h1: Can a homeowner do electrical, plumbing or gas work in Newton, MA?
title: Electrical, Plumbing & Gas Permits in Newton: Homeowner Rules
description: What Newton and Massachusetts say about who can pull electrical, plumbing and gas permits, which minor plumbing repairs need no permit, and water heater permits.
short_answer: Newton's electrical and plumbing/gas permit submissions require an appropriately signed license. Massachusetts issues plumbing permits only to licensed plumbers. The state lists minor repairs, such as fixing a leaky faucet or clearing a blocked drain, as not needing a permit.

facts.text: Electrical permit submissions require an appropriately signed electrical license.
Electrical submissions need liability insurance and workers' compensation unless the applicant is a sole proprietor.
Plumbing and gas submissions require an appropriately signed plumbing or gas license.
Replacing a gas water heater requires both a plumbing permit and a gas permit.
Massachusetts issues plumbing permits only to licensed plumbers.
Only licensed professionals may install, remove or repair plumbing.
Fixing a leaky faucet, valve or other working part, or clearing a blocked drain, is a minor repair that does not need a permit.
Licensed master or journeyman plumbers may do gas fitting, but a gas-fitter license does not cover plumbing work.

qa.q: Can I pull my own plumbing permit in Massachusetts?
qa.a: The state says plumbing permits are issued only to licensed plumbers.

qa.q: Do I need a permit to fix a leaky faucet?
qa.a: No. The state lists fixing a leaky faucet, valve or other working part, or clearing a blocked drain, as minor repairs that need no permit.

qa.q: What permits does a gas water heater replacement need in Newton?
qa.a: Both a plumbing permit and a gas permit.

qa.q: What does a Newton electrical permit application need?
qa.a: An appropriately signed electrical license, plus liability insurance and workers' compensation unless the applicant is a sole proprietor.

qa.q: Can a gas fitter do plumbing?
qa.a: No. The state says a gas-fitter license does not authorize plumbing work.
